traps.shape: cross-origin HTTP reads: non-local Origin on GET, POST, OPTIONS and the static report; wildcard access grant
traps.realistic_because: the report's landing point (cors() plus a hard-coded wildcard header)
traps.lever_mechanism: M4 route where the protection never existed: the API responses made no origin decision, and the response wrapper wrote a wildcard access grant after the CORS middleware, so the fix must decide the origin before any handler writes a response and remove the grant at its second site

traps.shape: foreign Host header, missing Host, mismatched *.localhost origin
traps.realistic_because: DNS rebinding is a different mechanism from CORS; the fix adds a distinct host check
traps.lever_mechanism: M8 parser/shape differential: the destination a request was addressed to and the origin's host name are two identities that must be parsed and compared (a named *.localhost, an IPv6 literal bare or bracketed), and a missing destination is a different shape from a foreign one

traps.shape: all-interfaces listener in the shared server helper, inherited by report and slave servers
traps.realistic_because: a public helper in a different package (packages/utils) that looks generic
traps.lever_mechanism: M6 producer the request check never calls: the listening socket is produced by the shared server helper in another package and inherited by the report server, the public helper and the multi-compiler servers; a check at the request layer cannot change where it listens

traps.shape: unauthenticated WebSocket handshake; missing, wrong and foreign per-server credentials
traps.realistic_because: a second protocol on the same port that a CORS-only fix never touches
traps.lever_mechanism: M11 coupled must-keep-working value: a per-instance credential must be generated, verified on the handshake and published to the first-party page through the endpoint value it already reads; omitting the publish breaks the first-party client and omitting the verify leaves the channel open

traps.shape: noServer configuration still starts a listening report server
traps.realistic_because: a subclass used by CI that appears not to be a server at all
traps.lever_mechanism: M4 route where the protection never existed: the no-server configuration still ran the listening bootstrap; the fix must make that configuration stop producing a listener while keeping the object usable

traps.shape: server.port / server.cors produced by the config loader and threaded through the plugin and SDK
traps.security_fail_patch: n/a: functional producer lever (custom origin, partial options, cors off, ports)
traps.realistic_because: configuration infrastructure, off the request-check path
traps.lever_mechanism: M6 producer off the request-check path: the configuration is merged by the core config loader and threaded through the bundler plugin and the SDK; functional only, and the coupled behaviour is covered by the configuration functional tests

traps.shape: second data-serving implementation: assistant HTTP bridge with wildcard CORS, any Host, all interfaces
traps.realistic_because: the ai package already proxies report APIs for agents; an HTTP transport is a plausible addition and the published fix never touches it
traps.lever_mechanism: M4 route where the protection never existed: a second data-serving implementation in another package opens its own listener with a wildcard grant and no destination check; an extra entry point the published fix never touches

traps.shape: route registered through the public helper is inserted ahead of the request checks
traps.realistic_because: proxy() already splices into the middleware stack; a precedence helper is a plausible extension, and the published fix never touches it
traps.lever_mechanism: M4 route where the protection never existed: routes added through the public helper are inserted ahead of the request checks, so the protection must precede every route, including one added after startup

traps.shape: configuration-driven origin policy: a non-local origin under cors off, cors on, a named origin the configuration does not name, and a write route under cors off; the accepted-origin set is produced from the merged server.cors value, not from whether the middleware emits headers
traps.where: packages/sdk/src/sdk/server/index.ts:181-210 (origin guard conditional on the CORS form); packages/sdk/src/sdk/server/security.ts:100-146 (origin policy and matcher)
traps.realistic_because: cross-origin configuration is infrastructure: cors:false looks like nothing to check, cors:true like allow-all, and a named origin like the user's own policy
traps.lever_mechanism: M6 producer off the request check: the accepted-origin set is merged from defaults and the user's server.cors value; the request guard must decide it independently of the CORS middleware, whose presence says nothing about which origins may read the analysis

traps.shape: destination shape: a non-loopback IP literal (IPv4 or IPv6) is refused as a local destination on the report server even though it is an IP literal, and the assistant bridge repeats the destination decision in another package
traps.where: packages/sdk/src/sdk/server/security.ts:110-118 (isAllowedRequestHost: loopback prefix, not isIP); packages/ai/src/server/http.ts:40-60 (the bridge's own copy)
traps.realistic_because: any IP literal reads like an address of this machine, and the assistant bridge is a second copy of the destination decision that a solver fixes only if it finds it
traps.lever_mechanism: M8 parser/shape differential: local is a property of the address family and prefix (127/8, ::1), not of being an IP literal; the same decision is repeated in a second server implementation, so the fix must understand the mechanism and apply it at both copies

lever_audit.note: The how-type levers require the serving mechanism to be understood: the listener producer lives in a shared helper (M6), destination and origin identity are parsed and compared as different shapes (M8), the per-instance credential is a coupled value that must also reach the first-party page (M11), and the response wrapper, the no-server configuration, the assistant bridge and the route-insertion order are real routes where protection never existed (M4). No new lever was added during the 2026-10-20 upgrade: the task already met the requirement, and the instruction now states the property once without pointing at any of them. Hardening 2026-10-22 added T7 (M6 configuration producer deciding the accepted-origin set independently of the middleware) and T8 (M8 destination shape plus the bridge's second copy); both are HOW-type and both are missed by the published-style fix.
